Hi Jordan / Priya / Marissa apologies for the slightly long note, wanted to give concrete steps so your engineers can start implementation without back-and-forth. Attaching an integration checklist + sample request snippets.

High-level integration plan (recommended):
1) Auth & access
   - API keys (recommended for POC); we can provision scoped keys limited to sandbox models.
   - For dedicated/private customers we support mTLS + KMS.
2) SDKs & quickstart
   - Official SDKs: JavaScript (npm @redwood/inference) and Python (pip redwood-inference).
   - Quickstart: 2 files: install SDK, set REDWOOD_API_KEY, call client.generate() / client.stream().
3) API routes (examples)
   - POST /v1/generate  synchronous text generation (JSON request with messages or prompt).
   - POST /v1/stream  streaming endpoint (SSE / chunked transfer encoding) that returns event chunks with token/delta fields.
   - POST /v1/embeddings  for embedding vectors (if you plan semantic search).
   - POST /v1/call-tool  structured tool-calling pattern we recommend for external routing (see below).
4) Streaming behavior
   - Streaming returns partial deltas as they’re generated. Client should reassemble token deltas; we provide SDK helpers to convert stream -> text.
   - For agent UI, render partial answers as soon as first stable sentence arrives; fallback to full response if streaming drops.
5) Tool / function calling (routing integration)
   - We support JSON-schema-style function definitions in the request. Runtime will return a call object with name + args. Example schema: {"name":"route_ticket","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"queue":{"type":"string"}}}}
   - On receiving a call, your service executes routing logic and returns a tool result to the model via /v1/call-tool response patch.
6) Rate limits & batching
   - Sandbox will have soft limit ~100 QPS; we recommend client-side exponential backoff on 429.
   - Batching: for short-context requests, use small batching in the agent aggregator to improve throughput.
7) Observability & evaluation
   - We’ll provide per-request latency/cost tokens in response headers. Redwood Console will show token-level breakdowns and per-route dashboards.

Security / infra notes:
- If ACME runs requests from behind a corporate NAT, whitelist Redwood IPs or use outbound proxy.
- CORS: browser-based integrations should use our browser SDK with token exchange; avoid placing long-lived keys in the browser.

Sample timeline (suggested):
- Week of Nov 8: provisioning + sample keys; initial smoke test with SDK.
- Week of Nov 15: technical kickoff and integration sprint (2-3 days).
- Week of Nov 22: internal eval and metrics collection.
- Week of Nov 29: POC wrap-up and go/no-go decision.

Attachments included: integration_checklist.pdf, sample_request_snippets.txt

for await (const chunk of stream) { renderPartial(chunk.delta); }
